gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-faculty-glyphic: Faculty Glyphic reads friendly and rounded, with generous openings in its bowls. Under Bruno Ace's ruler-straight heading, a long run of it keeps moving smoothly, since its strokes vary in weight where the heading's never do.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-fahkwang: Sleek and techy up top, with Bruno Ace drawing every stem, bowl and tail like rope, then Fahkwang below with faint pen-pressure shifts. Its rope-like consistency is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-figtree: Bruno Ace stretches out in lingering, ruler-drawn lines, while Figtree below looks marker-drawn, its e left wide open at the end. Paragraphs of it should feel loose and friendly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-finlandica: Bruno Ace draws its heading with one ruler-straight line and counters that stay connected to the outside, giving it a lingering, one-character-per-beat stride. Finlandica answers it with a constant-width outline you can trace by finger, which makes the pair feel tidy.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-fustat: Playful yet modern, Fustat bends its lines like tubing. Over a longer stretch, the wide gap where each c ends keeps the text light and easy to move through, under Bruno Ace's ruler-drawn heading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gantari: Bruno Ace keeps its counters connected to the outside. Gantari below looks bent from wire, with wide c apertures, so a long read feels friendly and unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-google-sans: Google Sans shows no thick-thin shift at all, its terminals pulled well back. Bruno Ace earns its place when set big and short, where its constant ruler-drawn line and lingering rhythm get room.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-google-sans-flex: Sharp, drawn-by-ruler lines up top, in Bruno Ace's distinctive display cut. Google Sans Flex follows with stroke ends that look cut from one ribbon, and that shared crispness is what ties them together.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gothic-a1: Bruno Ace is flat and unmodulated, every line ruler-drawn with counters left open to the outside. Gothic A1 follows with its splayed c terminal, and its low contrast keeps a longer read steady and approachable.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gotu: Flat, unmodulated strokes give Bruno Ace a distinctive, ruler-drawn look, and it does best as a lingering display voice. Gotu, though, has a sensible thick-thin difference and sturdy hairlines, which is what makes it the better fit for body text.
